artifacts.summary: Six-phase plan adding a repo-declared, build-free derived-artifact staleness probe plus a derived-output containment exemption to both implement-postflight engines.

memory_candidates.content: In this agent system both implement-postflight engines write the task status BEFORE creating the cycle's own git commit: orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh transitions status at WORK (f) (~line 1125) but commits at WORK (i) (~line 1755), and command-gate-out.sh calls update-task-status.sh before its artifact-validation and verification-hook stages. Consequently any gate that must prevent a task from reporting 'implemented' has to be evaluated BEFORE the status write, against the agent's reported modified_files and the still-uncommitted working tree -- it cannot be appended after the commit or wired into an extension lifecycle hook (every hook call site is unconditionally non-blocking and runs after the status write). The established isolation pattern for such a gate is a single boolean computed once and read only in the status-write arm, the verdict case, and the commit-message case (deploy_pending_refusal is the model). Separately, every pre-existing drift/staleness check in this codebase (file_scope excursion advisory, lifecycle hooks, lean-challenge-snapshot.sh --check) is deliberately advisory-only, so a blocking gate is a conscious documented departure rather than an incremental extension.
